Devon to schedule a 60m benchmark deep-dive for their model workload
Customer to share sample telemetry and retention policy requirements

Devon Patel: Prepare preliminary benchmark plan and sample harness questions (due 2027-06-07)
Omar Ruiz: Share current retention/PII policy and sample request volume estimates (due 2027-06-08)
header: Date: 2027-06-03 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE); Daniel Kwon (CTO, AeroForge), Lena Morales (Head of Security), Omar Ruiz (Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Procurement)
summary: Discovery call focused on AeroForge's security requirements for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logging granularity, BYOK/KMS options, and data retention/erasure policies. Redwood AE/SE outlined deployment modes and next steps: send security artifacts, schedule benchmark deep-dive, and gather AeroForge retention/telemetry samples.
topics: Encryption at rest / BYOK / KMS options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, appreciate it. We wanted to run through your security and deployment requirements and outline options between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated and Private.
[00:12] Daniel Kwon: Thanks, Maya. Quick intro — I'm Daniel, CTO at AeroForge. We're evaluating a couple providers but security is the gating factor for us, so we want to be thorough. Lena will drive the security questions.
[00:25] Lena Morales: Hi all. Yes, main things — SOC 2 and ISO evidence, how SSO and SAML flows map to RBAC, audit log fidelity, and what options you have for encryption and key management. Also retention and deletion guarantees for PII.
[00:40] Devon Patel: Totally — I'll start with a high-level and then we can get into specifics. For SOC2/ISO we have third-party attestations; we can share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate. Those are available in the security pack we usually send.
[00:58] Priya Shah: And will that be enough for procurement? We need the reports plus a short summary of controls.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include an executive summary and our control matrix. I'll attach the pack after the call.
[01:14] Omar Ruiz: On KMS — can you describe your BYOK options? We have a strict rule about not having cloud-managed keys for certain datasets.
[01:24] Devon Patel: We support BYOK for Redwood Private and Dedicated via customer-managed KMS. For Hosted, we offer envelope encryption with our KMS—but for regulated datasets we recommend Private or Dedicated with BYOK/HSM integration. Also we can do an HSM-backed flow with AWS KMS import for keys.
[01:46] Lena Morales: For the Hosted plan, how do you handle separation of tenant data? Is it multi-tenant at the inference layer or logical separation only?
[01:55] Ravi Singh: Hosted is multi-tenant with strong logical isolation, per-tenant encryption keys, and customer-scoped audit logs. Dedicated provides a reserved GPU pool and VPC peering so it's physically separated from other tenants. Private gives you a customer-install in your VPC or on-prem with full control.
[02:14] Daniel Kwon: What's the minimum SLA on Dedicated, and do you have SOC controls for deployment automation and change management?
[02:22] Devon Patel: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll send the SLA doc. Change management is covered in our SOC 2 controls — deployment automation, CI/CD pipelines, and separation of duties are documented in the control matrix.
[02:36] Lena Morales: Audit logs — we need per-request logs including request-id, model variant, prompt hash (or fingerprint), response latency, and redaction flags. Can Redwood provide that level of granularity and retention options? We also need to export logs to our SIEM.
[02:52] Devon Patel: We provide structured audit logs at the request level. You can choose retention windows and export via S3 or streaming to your SIEM (Kafka/Delivery). For privacy we can offer prompt hashing and token-level redaction policies. Exported logs can be pushed to your S3 bucket with SSE-KMS encryption.
[03:12] Omar Ruiz: About prompt hashing — can you guarantee non-reversible hashes for PII fields? We plan to run some regulatory checks.
[03:19] Devon Patel: We typically do SHA-256 hashing with salt rotation and can offer field-level tokenization prior to storage on Dedicated/Private. For Hosted there are policy-level redaction options.
[03:29] Priya Shah: On SSO: we use Okta, and SAML flows. Do you support Just-in-Time provisioning and SCIM for user sync?
[03:38] Ravi Singh: Yes — we support SAML2.0 SSO, IDP-initiated, SP-initiated flows, JIT provisioning for Hosted and Dedicated via our Console. SCIM for user sync is available on Dedicated and Private. RBAC is role-based mapped to groups from the IdP.
[03:53] Lena Morales: Need to validate least-privilege — ability to create roles limited to 'model inference', 'billing view', 'admin'. Also ephemeral tokens for service-to-service calls.
[04:04] Devon Patel: You can define custom roles in the Console and bind to SCIM groups. We also support short-lived service tokens with KMS-backed signing. For high-security setups our Private deployment supports certificate-based mTLS between services.
[04:19] Daniel Kwon: Any customer references in aerospace or manufacturing? It helps for our compliance team.
[04:25] Maya Chen: We can share anonymized reference cases — a couple regulated manufacturing customers on Dedicated and Private. I'll include contactable references in the pack.
[04:34] Omar Ruiz: Regarding data residency: we need EU-only processing for a subset of models. Can you route inference to specific regions and ensure logs never leave region?
[04:45] Devon Patel: Yes, routing policies support region pinning. For Hosted we have EU regions with data residency guarantees; Dedicated/Private give you finer control over where compute and logs live. We'll document cross-region fallback policies.
[04:58] Lena Morales: Incident response — we need playbooks and a timeline for breach notification.
[05:04] Ravi Singh: We have a published incident response plan with typical RTO/RPO, notification timelines, and post-incident reporting. For customers under contract we offer an escalation path and dedicated CSM/SE triage.
[05:19] Daniel Kwon: Are SOC2 gaps common in early-stage infra changes? I mean, if we run a POC and then go Dedicated will there be re-auditing overhead?
[05:29] Maya Chen: Transitioning from Hosted to Dedicated/Private doesn't require a full SOC 2 re-audit for you — our attestations cover the platform, and Dedicated/Private contractual addendums cover customer-specific controls. We'll lay it out in the security pack.
[05:44] Priya Shah: Procurement question — pricing model for Dedicated vs Private and minimum commit?
[05:50] Maya Chen: We'll include an indicative pricing sheet. Dedicated has reserved GPU commit tiers; Private is licensed with a one-time platform fee plus support. Details to follow with the commercial SE.
[06:01] Omar Ruiz: One more technical — audit log schema, is it JSON lines with structured fields? How easy to query?
[06:09] Devon Patel: Yes, logs are JSONL with indexed fields for request-id, user-id, model, tokens_generated, latencies. You can export to your ELK or Splunk, or query in Console for recent windows.
[06:22] Lena Morales: Retention windows — can we set different retention per log type (access logs 1 year, prompt logs 90 days)? Also immediate deletion on request for user data?
[06:33] Ravi Singh: You can configure retention per class: access logs, prompts, embeddings. For deletion we support data erasure requests; on Dedicated/Private we can do immediate purge. Hosted requests are processed per policy with audit trail of erasure.
[06:49] Daniel Kwon: Good. For the benchmark deep-dive, we want to run our 2 model types: short chatty dialog model and a long-context summarizer. Will you provision a test harness?
[06:59] Devon Patel: We'll put together a harness and suggest batching/quantization configs. For Dedicated we can run a small pilot on reserved nodes for more realistic latency.
[07:10] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps: I'll send the security pack, Rav i will add SCIM/SAML docs, Devon will prepare benchmark plan. Omar you'll share retention numbers and sample telemetry.
[07:22] Priya Shah: Sounds good. Any blockers before we schedule the benchmark deep dive?
[07:26] Daniel Kwon: No blockers, just need the security artifacts and the benchmark plan.
[07:33] Maya Chen: Perfect, we'll aim to get those over in the next few days. Thanks everyone.
[07:38] Lena Morales: Thanks, appreciate it. Bye.
[07:41] (call ends)
